levels.4: used in an episode and held up on review

skills.name: Timing and spacing
evidence: bench-bump v4: 10 camera moves vs 12, holds 3+ = 0
criteria: key poses land on the same frames as the reference (within 1 frame)
no unintended holds of 3+ frames
spacing eases where the reference eases

skills.name: Breath on held poses
evidence: retrofitted in all 13 Reels; still frames 1-9%
criteria: every held pose moves slightly (head and lean)
still steps under 10%

skills.name: Line boil on twos
criteria: outlines shift every 2 frames
boil never makes shapes unreadable

skills.name: Anticipation and follow-through
criteria: a readable wind-up before every main action
parts settle after the action (overshoot, then rest)
the reaction lands about 3 frames after the action

skills.name: Impact anatomy
evidence: bench-stick take 2-6; punch-in and 3-frame hold in A04, A09, A12
criteria: creep-in, smear frame, 3-frame contact hold
sparks or burst on contact
camera punch-in on the hit

skills.name: Smears and ghost trails
criteria: fast moves (more than a body width per frame) get a smear or ghosts
ghosts fade within 3 frames

skills.name: Effect mass (zaps, bursts, dust)
evidence: bench-zap v3: timing matched, effect too thin and small
criteria: the effect covers about the same share of the frame as the reference
effect strands cluster at the source and the target
the effect is redrawn every frame
burst blocks are as large as the reference's

skills.name: Stick strike
criteria: coil, wind-up, smear, contact hold, fold
the hit victim's head snaps back first

skills.name: Flight and landing
criteria: hang time at the top of the arc
flat landing, then bounce and dust
arms lag the body

skills.name: Run cycle
criteria: per-leg phase, on twos
about 45 degrees of lean
arms counter-swing

skills.name: Clinch and contact
criteria: arms aim at the contact point
silhouettes never tangle

skills.name: Camera grammar
criteria: push and pull alternate
accelerate into a transition, decelerate out
camera move count within 20% of the reference

skills.name: Motion inside the picture
evidence: bench-bump v7: local motion 4.6% vs reference 7.6%
criteria: local motion within 25% of the reference
many small independent movers, not one big one

skills.name: Faces built from forms
evidence: owner: face too generic; bench-bump v3 forms and tone planes
criteria: face reads at full size with forms (brow, nose, cheek, jaw)
2-4 flat tone planes
compared at full size, never from thumbnails

skills.name: Hard cel tone planes
criteria: 2-4 hard-edged tones per form
no soft gradients on characters

skills.name: Lived-in environment
evidence: bench-zap: room sparse vs reference picture, dresser, rug, curtains, motes
criteria: 3+ props that say where we are
a moving trace in the background (motes, light)
background never competes with the subject

skills.name: Two-character staging
evidence: A11: separate silhouettes, reaction 3 frames after action
criteria: about a body width between characters
one character acts while the other reacts

skills.name: Dialogue comedy grammar
criteria: establishing shot, then over-the-shoulder cuts
close-up on the punchline, then a reaction shot
a callback at the end
cuts land on the line, not after it

skills.name: Acting through expression
criteria: the expression changes before the line, not on it
brows and mouth disagree when the character lies or hides
eye direction tells us who they are thinking about

skills.name: Secondary action and overlap
criteria: loose parts (hair, cloth, props) drag 2-4 frames behind
a secondary action supports the main one without competing

skills.name: Logline and premise
criteria: one sentence: who, wants what, what stands in the way, why it's funny or matters
the premise has an engine that can make more than one scene
an outsider can retell it after one read

skills.name: Character want, need and flaw
criteria: each lead wants something concrete on screen
the flaw causes the trouble
the want is visible in action, not stated

skills.name: Setup and payoff
criteria: every payoff was planted earlier and visible on screen
every plant pays off
the plant is disguised as something else when it appears

skills.name: Rule of three (pattern, pattern, break)
criteria: two beats set a pattern
the third breaks it in a surprising but fair way
the break is the shortest beat

skills.name: Escalation
criteria: each beat raises the stakes or absurdity over the last
no beat repeats the same level
the top is reached just before the end

skills.name: Reversal and twist
criteria: the twist recontextualises earlier beats
rewatching shows it was planted
the twist comes from character, not coincidence

skills.name: Joke craft: misdirection and the turn
criteria: the setup leads to an expected meaning
the punch word/image arrives last
the turn is understood in under a second

skills.name: Running gag and callback
criteria: the gag appears at least three times, changed each time
the final callback tops the earlier ones
a newcomer still gets the last one

skills.name: Irony, deadpan and contradiction
criteria: words and action contradict on screen
the deadpan character never signals the joke
another character or the chorus voices the reaction

skills.name: Dialogue with subtext
criteria: no line states the character's feeling directly
each line is something a real person would say
the scene works with the sound off (action carries meaning)

skills.name: Three-act structure (micro)
criteria: setup, confrontation, resolution are each visible
the turn into act 2 is a choice by the lead
the resolution answers the opening question

skills.name: Kishotenketsu (intro, development, twist, reconcile)
criteria: four beats: introduce, develop, an unrelated-seeming turn, reconciliation
the story works without a villain or conflict
the reconcile links beat 3 back to beats 1-2

skills.name: Hook and cold open (first second)
criteria: something changes or is wrong in the first second
the question it raises is answered only at the end
no title, logo or setup before the hook

skills.name: Curiosity gap and mystery
criteria: an open question is planted early
clues are fair and visible
the answer is surprising yet inevitable

skills.name: Suspense (the audience knows more)
criteria: the audience sees the danger the character doesn't
time pressure is visible
release comes from character action

skills.name: Heartfelt emotional arc
criteria: the lead ends in a different emotional state
the change is shown in one concrete action
no music or narration tells us how to feel

skills.name: Horror-lite tension and release
criteria: a normal space becomes wrong in small steps
the scare is set up by silence or stillness
comedy release follows the peak (for our tone)

skills.name: Hero's journey (compressed)
criteria: call, refusal or doubt, threshold, ordeal, return each present
the return brings something back
fits the target length without rushing a beat

skills.name: Explainer story (Think!)
criteria: opens on the viewer's problem
one mechanism explained through a concrete scene
the viewer leaves knowing what to do

skills.name: Series format (story on rails)
criteria: the same beat grammar works for three different premises
what changes per episode is named
the format is recognisable within 2 seconds

skills.name: Endings: button, topper and loop
criteria: the last beat is the strongest or a quiet button after it
a loop ending flows into the first frame
nothing happens after the payoff
